quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 40 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: When carrying a load on your motorcycle, where should it be secured?
questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible.
questions.explanation: Loads should be secured as low as possible. Attaching a load to a sissy bar raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and can upset its balance.

questions.question: What is the key to making a quick turn on a motorcycle?

options.text: Get your motorcycle to lean quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get your motorcycle to lean quickly.
questions.explanation: To make a quick turn, you must get your motorcycle to lean quickly in the direction you want to turn. The sharper the turn, the more the motorcycle must lean.

questions.question: A motorcycle's brake light is _________ a passenger vehicle's brake light.
questions.correctAnswerText: Not as noticeable as
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is usually not as noticeable as a larger vehicle's brake light, especially when the taillight is on. Other drivers may not see your brake light, so stay aware.

questions.question: In California, a motorized scooter can be operated by someone with:
questions.correctAnswerText: Any class of driver license.
questions.explanation: In California, anyone with any class of driver license can operate a motorized scooter.

questions.question: Traffic lanes moving in the same direction are separated by:
questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid white lines mean you cannot pass. Dashed white lines mean you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: It connects the front and rear brakes together when you apply the rear brake.
It automatically applies the brakes based on your riding habits.
It applies the brake automatically when you downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: It connects the front and rear brakes together when you apply the rear brake.
questions.explanation: An integrated braking system links the front and rear brakes together when you use the rear brake pedal. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: To get the most protection from your helmet, it should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snugly.
questions.explanation: Your helmet gives you the best protection when it meets DOT standards, fits snugly all the way around, and has no damage.

questions.question: When sitting on a motorcycle, you should position yourself so you can:

options.text: Use your arms to support your body weight.
Sit at an angle to help support your weight with your arms.
Use your arms to control the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your arms to control the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Sit with a posture that lets you use your arms to control your motorcycle. Your arms should not have to hold up your body or support your weight.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of the road with its lights flashing. You should:

options.text: Stop on the roadway behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait until the emergency vehicle starts moving.
Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside assistance vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes to give it extra space. Slow down and be ready to stop as you pass the emergency scene.

questions.question: When motorcyclists ride in a group, where should inexperienced riders be positioned?

options.text: Near the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the front of the group.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride near the front of the group, behind the leader. This allows experienced riders to lead the way and watch the inexperienced riders at the same time.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid getting tired on a long motorcycle trip?
questions.correctAnswerText: Take breaks often to rest.
questions.explanation: To avoid tiredness on long trips, limit your riding time each day and take frequent breaks. Do not use stimulants because you may feel very tired when they wear off.

questions.question: What does it mean when you make eye contact with another driver?

options.text: It does not mean they will give you the right of way.
They will definitely give you the right of way.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not mean they will give you the right of way.
questions.explanation: Never assume that eye contact with another driver means they will give you the right of way. A driver may look right at you and still not see you.

questions.question: What does your steering feel like if your front tire goes flat?
questions.correctAnswerText: Heavy.
questions.explanation: If steering suddenly feels heavy, your front tire may be flat. Stop and check your tires right away.

questions.question: How should motorcyclists ride in a group on a straight road?
questions.correctAnswerText: In a staggered pattern.
questions.explanation: A staggered pattern is the best way to keep the group close while giving each rider enough space. Switch to a single-file line when turning, riding through curves, or entering or leaving the road.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid danger, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the front brake while swerving.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Do one action first, then the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action first, then the other.
questions.explanation: When you need to brake and swerve, do these actions separately. Never brake while swerving because it can make your motorcycle tip over.

questions.question: When should you use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch?

options.text: When the throttle is stuck and you cannot free it.
When you start to lose control in a curve.
When the motorcycle starts to wobble.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the throttle is stuck and you cannot free it.
questions.explanation: If the throttle gets stuck and you cannot free it, use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch right away. This will stop power to the rear wheel so you can safely leave the road and stop.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a turn?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down before you enter a turn. Taking a turn too fast can cause you to drift out of your lane or off the road.

questions.question: What should a rider always do to turn safely?

options.text: Lean in the direction of the curve.
Turn by using only the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean in the direction of the curve.
questions.explanation: Always lean in the direction of the turn. Slow down before you enter the turn.

questions.question: Where should you ride in your lane when being passed?

options.text: In the left part of the lane.
In the center part of the lane.
In the right part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center part of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, the center of the lane is usually the safest spot. Riding on the side near the passing vehicle increases crash risk. Riding on the far side can make the other driver return to your lane unsafely.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist do in high-risk areas?

options.text: Hold the clutch and brake levers ready to react faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the clutch and brake levers ready to react faster.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like intersections, shopping centers, schools, or construction zones, slow down. Hold the clutch and both brake levers ready so you can react quickly in an emergency.

questions.question: Why should you not ride directly next to another vehicle?

options.text: Another driver may want to use your lane to pass.
You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
You may have access to escape routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous. The driver may not see you in their blind spot. Also, the vehicle may block your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: A plastic face shield can protect you from:
questions.correctAnswerText: Dust.
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your face in a crash. It also shields you from everyday hazards like rocks from other vehicles, wind, dust, dirt, rain, and insects.

questions.question: What color are service signs?
questions.correctAnswerText: Blue with white letters.
questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show where services are located. These include rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift located on a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: By the left footrest.
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
Drivers may proceed through the intersection with caution.
Drivers must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red light. You must stop completely and wait for a signal that allows you to turn in your desired direction.

questions.question: Why does a motorcycle rider have an advantage when passing parked vehicles?

options.text: The motorcycle can accelerate more quickly than a car.
The motorcyclist can ride in the left part of the lane to avoid people and cars to their right.
Motorcycles have a shorter stopping distance than cars do.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcyclist can ride in the left part of the lane to avoid people and cars to their right.
questions.explanation: When parked vehicles are on your right, ride in the left part of your lane. This helps you avoid opening doors, people getting out, or people stepping between vehicles. Only do this if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Where is conflict between you and other vehicles most likely to happen?
questions.correctAnswerText: At an intersection
questions.explanation: Conflicts between motorcycles and other vehicles happen most often at intersections.

questions.question: Where do most motorcycle and car accidents occur?
questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections.
questions.explanation: Most crashes between motorcycles and cars happen at intersections. Usually, the car driver fails to give the right-of-way to the motorcycle.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Throttle down and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.question: What should you do when riding in the rain?

options.text: Ride down the center of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.
Ride in tire tracks left by other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in tire tracks left by other cars.
questions.explanation: Roads are slippery when rain first starts. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars to get better grip.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will be entering the roadway.
Stop completely and go only when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and go only when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must stop completely, check for other traffic and pedestrians, and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, tell them to:

options.text: Get on before you start the engine.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay quiet and still.
questions.explanation: Passengers should not talk or move while the motorcycle is moving. They should get on after the engine starts and sit as far forward as possible without crowding you.

questions.question: In normal conditions, how far back should you stay from the vehicle ahead?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep at least a two-second distance from the vehicle ahead under normal conditions. Use more distance when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The light is about to turn red.
The light is about to turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A yellow light warns that the signal is changing to red soon. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, go through it.

questions.question: When riding in a group, a staggered formation:

options.text: Should be used all the time.
Should not be used when entering or exiting a highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not be used when entering or exiting a highway.
questions.explanation: Staggered formation is usually good, but switch to single file when riding in curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: When riding in a group, all riders should:

options.text: Only the lead rider should check mirrors.
Not check mirrors because it is a distraction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check their mirrors often.
questions.explanation: All riders should check their mirrors often to watch the riders behind them and to make sure the group stays together.

questions.question: When should you check your motorcycle's safety?
questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Always check your motorcycle before you ride. Small problems on a motorcycle are more dangerous than small problems on a car.

questions.question: The best lane position should:

options.text: Help you see others and let them see you.
Place you in other drivers' blind spots.
Let other drivers share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see others and let them see you.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see other vehicles and lets them see you. It keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It also stops other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you a way to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: When entering a curve, position your motorcycle:

options.text: On the outside edge of the curve.
On the inside edge of the curve.
Where you can safely handle the road and traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where you can safely handle the road and traffic.
questions.explanation: Every curve is different. Choose a lane position that works for the conditions you face and change it as needed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This is a traffic law sign with white background, red, and black markings. It tells you that U-turns are not allowed in this area.
